source_text: ἰσχνῆς τὴν πολεμικὴν γενέσθαι σκευὴν, κίδαρίν τε καὶ ζώνην. Κόσμῳ μὲν οὖν ἱεροπρεπεῖ λαμπρόν τε καὶ ἀξιάγαστον ὑποφαίνει τὸν Ἀαρών. Προσεπιτάττει δὲ λέγων· «Καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἀαρὼν ποιήσεις χιτῶνας καὶ ζώνας, καὶ κιδάρεις ποιήσεις αὐτοῖς εἰς τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν. Καὶ ἐνδύσεις αὐτὰ Ἀαρὼν τὸν ἀδελφόν σου, καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ μετ' αὐτοῦ. Καὶ χρίσεις αὐτοὺς, καὶ ἐμπλήσεις αὐτῶν τὰς χεῖρας, καὶ ἁγιάσεις αὐτοὺς, ἵνα ἱερατεύωσί μοι. Καὶ ποιήσεις αὐτοῖς περισκελῆ λινᾶ καλύψαι ἀσχημοσύνην χρωτὸς αὐτῶν, ἀπὸ ὀσφύος ἕως μηρῶν ἔσται. Καὶ ἕξει Ἀαρὼν αὐτὰ καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ, ὅταν εἰσπορεύωνται εἰς τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου, ἢ ὅταν προσπορεύωνται λειτουργεῖν πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον τοῦ ἁγίου. Καὶ οὐκ ἐπάξονται πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς ἁμαρτίαν, ἵνα μὴ ἀποθάνωσι. Νόμιμον αἰώνιον αὐτῷ καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετ' αὐτόν.» Ὁρᾷς ὅτι καὶ αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἐξ Ἀαρὼν ἐμπρέπει τὸ, ὡς ἔν γε τῷ πολεμικῷ καθορᾶσθαι σχήματι. Μάχιμον γὰρ τὸ ἱερὸν ἅπαν ἐστὶ γένος, καὶ οὐ πρὸς αἷμα καὶ σάρκα στρατεύεσθαί τε καὶ ἀντεξάγειν εἰδὸς, ἀλλὰ τῆς βεβήλου κατακωλύειν ἁμαρτίας, ἐμφανέστατά τε καὶ λογικῶς τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας δογμάτων ὑπερμαχόμενον, καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζον πᾶν νόημα εἰς τὴν ὑπακοὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καθὰ γέγραπται. Περισκελές τε λινοῦν αὐτοῖς, τὸ ἀκαλλές τε καὶ ἄσχημον τῶν περὶ μηροὺς κατασκιάζον εὖ μάλα. Σεμνὰ γὰρ εὖ μάλα πάντα τὰ τῶν ἀγίων, καὶ ἄσχημον ἐν αὐτοῖς οὐδέν· ὑποσημαίνει δέ πως τὸ λινοῦν τοῖς περιμηροῖς τοῦ σώματος μέρεσιν ἐπενηνεγμένον, ὅτι τοῖς ἁγίοις πρεπωδεστάτη τῶν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡδονῶν ἡ ἀπόψυξις· ψυχρὸν γὰρ τὸ λινοῦν. Τὸ δὲ θερμὸν εἰς ὀρέξεις τὰς μυσαρωτάτας, ὁσίου παντὸς ἀλλότριον. Ἐκ λίνου δὲ καὶ ἑτέρως τοῖς ἱερᾶσθαι λαχοῦσιν, ἄμφιά τε καὶ περισκελῆ. Νεκρῶν γὰρ ἔργων ἀποφοιτᾷν ἀναγκαῖον αὐτούς· σύμβολον δὲ νεκρότητος ὡς ἐκ θνησειδίου ληφθὲν, φημὶ δὴ προβάτου. Νεκρῶν οὖν ἔργων ἀπόθεσις, ὡς ἐν τύπῳ πάλιν, τὸ τοῖς ἐκ λίνου ἐστάλθαι, καὶ οὐχὶ δὴ μᾶλλον τοῖς ἐξ ἐρίων ἐσθήμασι· καὶ τοῦτο νόμος ἅγιος ὁ διηνεκής. Ἕψεται δὲ ὅτι πάντη τε καὶ πάντως τὸ ἐκτεθνάναι δεῖν, ἠμεληκόσι τοῦ πρέποντος, Καὶ τῆς ὅτι μάλιστα πρεπούσης αὐτοῖς εὐκοσμίας, διαμεμήνυκεν εἰπὼν ὅ τι χρὴ φοροῦντας ἱερουργεῖν· Καὶ οὐκ ἐπάξονται, φησὶ, πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς ἁμαρτίαν, ἵνα μὴ ἀποθάνωσιν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀσφαλὴς ὁ νόμος τὸ ἑκάστῳ λυσιτελὲς εὖ μάλα καταδεικνὺς, καὶ τὰ δι' ὧν ἄριστα ἔχοι σαφῆ καθιστάς. {ΚΥΡ.} Ὧδε ἔχει· καὶ στολῇ μὲν τῇ τοιᾷδε τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἀπόλεκτον κατακαλλύνει γένος, ἁγιάζει δὲ καὶ ἑτέρως. ὡς ἐν σκιᾷ μὲν ἔτι, πλὴν ἐν Χριστῷ. Γέγραπται γὰρ δὲ ὡδί· «Καὶ ταῦτά ἐστιν ἃ ποιήσεις αὐτοῖς· ἁγίασαι αὐτοὺς ὥστε ἱερατεύειν μοι αὐτοὺς, λήψῃ μοσχάριον ἐκ βοῶν ἓν, καὶ κριοὺς δύο ἀμώμους, καὶ ἄρτους ἀζύμους πεφυραμένους ἐν ἐλαίῳ, καὶ λάγανα ἄζυμα κεχρισμένα ἐν ἐλαίῳ. Σεμίδαλιν ἐκ πυ
pass_a_gloss: [Cyril, continuing from §12] ...(that) from linen (βύσσος) alone, very thin (ἰσχνός), the war-gear (πολεμικὴ σκευή) came to be, headdress (κίδαρις) and sash (ζώνη). With priest-befitting adornment (κόσμος ἱεροπρεπής) he shows Aaron bright and admirable (ἀξιάγαστος). He commands further: [Exod 28:40-43 LXX] for Aaron's sons make tunics (χιτῶνες), sashes, caps (κιδάρεις) for honour (τιμή) and glory (δόξα); put them on Aaron your brother and his sons; anoint (χρίσεις), fill their hands (ἐμπλήσεις τὰς χεῖρας = ordain), sanctify (ἁγιάσεις) them so they serve me as priests (ἱερατεύωσι); make linen undergarments (περισκελῆ λινᾶ) to cover the shame (ἀσχημοσύνη) of their skin/body, from loins (ὀσφύς) to thighs (μηροί); Aaron and sons shall have them when they enter the tent of witness (σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου) or approach to minister (λειτουργεῖν) at the altar of the holy (place); and they will not bring sin (ἁμαρτία) upon themselves lest they die; perpetual statute (νόμιμον αἰώνιον) for him and his seed. You see it befits those from Aaron also to be seen as in warlike dress (σχῆμα πολεμικόν). For the whole sacred race (ἱερὸν γένος) is combative (μάχιμος), knowing how to campaign (στρατεύεσθαι) and march out (ἀντεξάγειν) not against blood and flesh, but to restrain profane (βέβηλος) sin, fighting for (ὑπερμαχόμενον) the doctrines (δόγματα) of the truth most openly and rationally (λογικῶς), and taking captive (αἰχμαλωτίζον) every thought (νόημα) into the obedience (ὑπακοή) of Christ, as written. Linen undergarment for them, shading over the unlovely and unseemly about the thighs. For all things of the saints are very dignified (σεμνά), nothing unseemly in them; the linen laid on the thigh-parts hints that cooling (ἀπόψυξις) of the pleasures (ἡδοναί) of the flesh is most fitting for saints, for linen is cold; the hot toward most abominable appetites (ὀρέξεις μυσαρώταται) is alien to all holy (ὅσιος). Also otherwise those allotted to be priests have robes (ἄμφια) and undergarments of linen: they must depart from dead works (νεκρὰ ἔργα); symbol of deadness (νεκρότης) as taken from a carcass (θνησείδιον), I mean a sheep [i.e. wool]. So putting off (ἀπόθεσις) dead works, as in a type (τύπος), is being clad in linen and not rather in woollen (ἐρίων) garments; and this the holy perpetual (διηνεκής) law. It will follow that by all means one must die if neglecting the fitting (τὸ πρέπον) and the good order (εὐκοσμία) most befitting them: he indicated, having said what they must wear to do sacred service (ἱερουργεῖν): they will not bring sin on themselves lest they die. [Palladius] The law is safe/sure (ἀσφαλής), showing well what profits (λυσιτελές) each, and making clear the means by which things would be best. [Cyril] So it holds; with such a robe (στολή) he beautifies the sacred and chosen (ἀπόλεκτον) race, but sanctifies (ἁγιάζει) also otherwise, as in shadow (σκιά) still, yet in Christ. For it is written: [Exod 29:1-2 LXX] these are the things you shall do for them: to sanctify them so they serve me as priests, take one calf (μοσχάριον) from cattle, two unblemished (ἄμωμοι) rams, unleavened loaves (ἄρτοι ἄζυμοι) kneaded in oil, unleavened wafers (λάγανα) anointed in oil; fine flour (σεμίδαλις) of wheat [continues in §14].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …thin, that his war gear was made, the headdress and the belt. So with adornment fit for a priest he shows Aaron splendid and admirable. Then he gives a further command, saying: ‘And for the sons of Aaron you shall make tunics and belts, and you shall make headdresses for them, for honor and glory. And you shall put them on Aaron your brother, and on his sons with him. And you shall anoint them, and ordain them, and sanctify them, so that they may serve me as priests. And you shall make for them linen undergarments to cover the nakedness of their bodies; they shall reach from the loins to the thighs. And Aaron and his sons shall wear them whenever they go into the tent of witness, or whenever they come near to minister at the altar of the sanctuary. And they shall not bring sin upon themselves, so that they do not die. It is a perpetual statute for him and for his offspring after him’ (Exodus 28:40–43). You see that it befits Aaron’s descendants too to be seen, as it were, in the dress of war. For the whole sacred race is made for battle. It knows how to campaign and take the field, not against blood and flesh (Ephesians 6:12), but so as to hold back profane sin, fighting most openly and with reason for the doctrines of the truth, and ‘taking every thought captive to the obedience of Christ’ (2 Corinthians 10:5), as it is written. They also have a linen undergarment, which covers very well what is unlovely and unseemly about the thighs. For all that belongs to the saints is truly dignified, and nothing unseemly is found in them. And the linen placed on the parts of the body around the thighs hints in some way that the cooling of the pleasures of the flesh is most fitting for the saints, for linen is cool. Heat that runs toward the most loathsome desires is foreign to everything holy. And there is another reason why those who have been allotted the priesthood wear robes and undergarments of linen. They must depart from dead works, and what is taken from a dead creature, I mean a sheep, is a symbol of deadness. So, again as in a type, to be clothed in garments of linen and not rather in garments of wool is the putting away of dead works; and this is the holy and perpetual law. And he made it plain that death must follow, wholly and without fail, for those who neglect what is fitting and the good order that most befits them, when, after saying what they must wear to perform the sacred service, he added: ‘And they shall not bring sin upon themselves, so that they do not die’ (Exodus 28:43).
Palladius: The law is sure. It shows very well what benefits each person, and it makes clear the means by which things would go best.

Cyril: So it is. With such a robe he adorns the sacred and chosen race, and he sanctifies it in another way as well: still as in shadow, yet in Christ. For it is written thus: ‘And these are the things you shall do for them to sanctify them, so that they may serve me as priests. You shall take one young bull from the herd and two unblemished rams, and unleavened loaves kneaded with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil. Of fine wheat flour…’ (Exodus 29:1–2)
